name: upstream-importer
description: Copies files from an upstream repository fetched under upstream/<name>/ into the project: a chosen set of paths, with optional renames and literal substitutions, modes preserved, binaries byte for byte. Code does the copying from a JSON spec in the task; no model is involved. The worker then runs the checks, commits and opens the pull request.
when_to_use: Bootstrapping a project from a template repository, vendoring documents or assets from a reference, or pulling a directory tree in from another repository that is registered as an upstream of this project (agentpipe projects upstream add). Not for files that must be written or adapted by hand: import them, then give docs-writer or coder a follow-up task on the imported copies. Not for fetching: the upstream must already be listed in the project.
inputs: A fenced ```json block holding the spec: {"upstream": "<name under upstream/>", "include": [globs relative to the upstream root], "exclude": [globs], "rename": {"src/prefix/": "dest/prefix/"}, "substitute": {"{{GAME}}": "Source of the Nile"}, "verbatim": [globs copied without substitution], "executable": [globs made mode 755], "overwrite": false}. Only upstream and include are required. Say in prose what the import is for and which files other tasks will adapt afterwards.
outputs: A branch with the imported files committed (one commit, message naming the upstream repository and commit), a pull request when the project pushes, and a report listing every file copied (with the substitutions applied), skipped or excluded, plus the upstream commit for provenance.
